subject: general
question: The Railways ordered which safety feature to be installed at stations in Pune in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Panic alert buttons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Railways** has issued a directive to install **Panic alert buttons** at various railway stations within the **Pune Division** to enhance passenger security, with a target completion date of **June 2025**.
 
• These buttons are specifically designed to act as an emergency signaling system for **women**, **children**, and **elderly passengers** who may find themselves in distress while on the platform.
 
• The system is directly integrated with the **Railway Protection Force (RPF)** control room; once the button is pressed, an alert is instantly generated, identifying the **exact location** of the passenger.
 
• This safety feature is part of the **Indian Railways'** ongoing efforts to modernize **station infrastructure** and provide a proactive response mechanism against crimes like **harassment** or **theft**.
 
• The initiative in **Pune** serves as a critical pilot for implementing **IoT-based security solutions** that bridge the gap between passengers and security personnel in real-time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pune Railway Division**: Falling under the **Central Railway** zone, it is one of the highest revenue-generating and busiest divisions in **Maharashtra**, making it a priority for safety upgrades.
 
• **Integrated Security System (ISS)**: The **Panic alert buttons** are a component of the broader **ISS**, which also includes **CCTV surveillance**, **baggage scanners**, and **metal detectors** to provide multi-layered protection.
 
• **Railway Protection Force (RPF)**: A specialized security force under the **Ministry of Railways**, the **RPF** is tasked with the protection of **railway property** and the safety of the **42 crore** (approximate) annual passengers using the network.
 
• **Meri Saheli Initiative**: This program works alongside physical safety features like buttons, where dedicated teams of **female RPF personnel** interact with solo women travelers to provide security throughout their journey.
 
• **Nirbhaya Fund**: Many such safety installations at **Indian Railways** stations are funded through the **Nirbhaya Fund**, a non-lapsable corpus established in **2013** for schemes aimed at improving **women's safety** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Response Mechanism**: Upon activation of the button, **Quick Reaction Teams (QRT)** of the **RPF** are expected to reach the spot within **3 to 5 minutes** to assist the passenger.
 
• **Technological Features**: Most modern **Panic alert buttons** installed by the railways are equipped with **two-way communication**, allowing the passenger to speak directly with the dispatcher while help is on the way.
 
• **Timeline**: The **June 2025** deadline set for **Pune** stations ensures that the technology is synced with the **Smart City** projects currently being implemented in the region.
 
• **Legal Context**: Under the **Railways Act, 1989**, ensuring the safety of passengers is a statutory duty, and the introduction of such devices helps the administration meet these legal and **ethical obligations**.
</ul
